Rashi on Menachot 10a:10:1.hebrew: ואידך שמאלית דעני - הכתוב מיותר, למאי אתא:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:10:1.english: And the other — the left [hand] of the poor [leper] - [The verse] is superfluous; for what purpose does it come?

Rashi on Menachot 10a:10:2.hebrew: שנתחדש בה - ופרשת עני נתחדש בה קרבן עולה ויורד:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:10:2.english: That was introduced in it - And in the passage of the poor person, the offering of a sliding scale [oleh veyored] was introduced.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:12:1.hebrew: קס"ד אצבע וכהונה בעינן - דלא אמרינן ימין אלא אם כן [כתיב] אצבע וכהונה, כגון חטאת דכתיב ביה ולקח הכהן מדם החטאת באצבעו (ויקרא ד׳:כ״ה) — ההיא ודאי ימנית הוא, דגמר ממצורע עשיר דכתיב ביה וטבל הכהן את אצבעו הימנית (ויקרא י״ד:ט״ז). מה אצבע וכהונה דהכא ימין, אף דעלמא נמי ימין:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:12:1.english: It entered our mind [to say] that we require a finger and priesthood - For we do not say "right hand" unless [the verse] says both "finger" and "priest," such as the sin offering, regarding which it is written: "And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger" (Leviticus 4:25) — that one is certainly the right [hand], since it is derived from the wealthy leper, regarding whom it is written: "And the priest shall dip his right finger" (Leviticus 14:16). Just as with [the case of] finger and priesthood here [in the leper] it is the right hand, so too elsewhere it is also the right hand.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:14:1.hebrew: ותנן - במסכת תמיד (דף לא:) בהולכת אברים: הרגל של ימין היה מוליך בשמאל. משום דאמרינן במסכת יומא (דף כה.) סדר אברים: הראש והרגל היה נושא בבת אחת, והאי רגל, מדאזיל בהדי רישא, ודאי רגל ימין הוא דחשיב. הלכך, הראש שהוא כבד וחשוב היה מוליך בימין, והירך בשמאל, ואע"ג דכתב בהו כהן:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:14:1.english: And we learned - In tractate Tamid (31b), regarding the conveyance of the limbs: he would carry the right foot in his left hand. This is because we say in tractate Yoma (25a) [regarding] the order of the limbs: he would carry the head and the foot together, and this foot, since it goes along with the head, is certainly the right foot, which is the more important one. Therefore, the head, which is heavy and important, he would carry in the right hand, and the thigh in the left, even though "the priest" is written regarding them.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:15:1.hebrew: ומשני לעולם או אצבע או כהונה - וכי אמרינן דבעינן "אינה אלא ימין", בדבר המעכב כפרה, דומיא דהזאות דמצורע. לאפוקי הולכה, דלא מעכבא, דאפשר לפשוט ולנתח אצל הכבש. אי נמי, אם יש כהנים הרבה, יושיטו זה לזה:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:15:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Actually, [the rule is] either finger or priesthood - And when we say [that the verse means] "it is only the right [hand]," [this applies] to a matter that precludes atonement, similar to the sprinklings of the leper. This excludes conveyance [of the limbs to the ramp], which does not preclude [atonement], since it is possible to skin and cut up [the animal] next to the ramp. Alternatively, if there are many priests, they can pass [the limbs] to one another.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:16:1.hebrew: והא קבלה דמעכבא כפרה - דאי אפשר שלא יתקבל הדם בכלי, וכתב בה כהונה: "והקריבו בני אהרן את הדם" (ויקרא א׳:ח׳), ואמרינן בתורת כהנים: "והקריבו" — זו קבלת הדם. ותנן: רבי שמעון מכשיר קבלה בשמאל:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:16:1.english: But [isn't there] the collection [of the blood], which is indispensable for atonement - For it is impossible for the blood not to be collected in a vessel, and [yet] priesthood is written regarding it: "And Aaron's sons shall present the blood" (Leviticus 1:8). And we say in the Torat Kohanim: "And they shall present" — this is the collection of the blood. And we learned [in a mishnah]: Rabbi Shimon deems fit a collection [done] with the left hand.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:17:1.hebrew: לרבי שמעון קאמרת - כלומר, מדרבי שמעון פרכת? בתמיה:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:17:1.english: Do you say [this] according to Rabbi Shimon? - That is, [do] you raise your objection from [the words of] Rabbi Shimon? [It is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:17:2.hebrew: תרתי בעי - אצבע וכהונה. וכי קאמר ריש לקיש "או אצבע או כהונה" — לרבנן קא אמר, דפסול:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:17:2.english: He requires two things - Finger and priesthood. And when Reish Lakish says, "either finger or priesthood" [is lacking, the offering is disqualified], he is speaking according to the Rabbis, who hold that [the offering] is disqualified.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:18:1.hebrew: יד אינה אלא ימין - דגמר מידו הימנית דמצורע [עשיר]:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:18:1.english: "Hand" is only the right - For it is derived from "the right hand" of the wealthy leper [i.e., the verse that mentions the right hand of a leper who brings the offering of a wealthy person].

Rashi on Menachot 10a:18:2.hebrew: ומשני אצבע לא בעיא כהונה - דהיכא דכתב אצבע, אע"ג דלא כתב כהן, אינו אלא ימין. ומשכחת לה באחרי מות: "ולקח מדם הפר והזה באצבעו", הרי אצבע בלא כהונה:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:18:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: A finger does not require priesthood - For where [the verse] wrote "finger," even though it did not write "priest," it is only the right [hand]. And you find this in [the portion of] Acharei Mot: "And he shall take of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger" (Leviticus 16:14) — behold, [there is] a finger without priesthood [being mentioned].

Rashi on Menachot 10a:18:3.hebrew: כהונה בעיא אצבע - לרבי שמעון, אף על גב דכתיב כהונה, לא אמרינן ״ימין״ אלא אם כן כתב אצבע. משום הכי מכשיר בקבלה:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:18:3.english: Priesthood requires finger - According to Rabbi Shimon, even though "priesthood" is written, we do not say [that it means the] right [hand] unless the verse also wrote "finger." Therefore, he deems [the service] valid with the receiving [of the blood done with the left hand, since the verse about receiving mentions only priesthood and not finger].

Rashi on Menachot 10a:19:1.english: In his priesthood - In the priestly garments.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:1:1.hebrew: חד - על בהן, בין דיד בין דרגל:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:1:1.english: One - [refers] to the thumb, both of the hand and of the foot.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:1:2.hebrew: להכשיר צדדין - של בהן, דדרשינן לקמן (מנחות דף צו.) "על" — בסמוך, כדכתיב: ועליו מטה מנשה:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:1:2.english: To permit the sides - of the thumb, for we derive below (Menachot 96a) that "upon" [means] adjacent, as it is written: "And upon him [shall be] the tribe of Manasseh."

Rashi on Menachot 10a:1:3.hebrew: וחד על - כתוב בהן, בין דיד בין דרגל, לפסול צידי צדדין — בשר התחתון שכנגד הכף, דעל אמרינן ולא תחת:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:1:3.english: And one [verse says] "upon" - [It is written] regarding the thumb, both of the hand and of the foot, to disqualify the sides of the sides — the lower flesh that is opposite the palm [of the hand or the sole of the foot], for we say "upon," and not "beneath."

Rashi on Menachot 10a:2:1.hebrew: על דם האשם - דעשיר. וכן ועל מקום דם האשם דעני:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:2:1.english: Upon the blood of the guilt offering - [This refers to the guilt offering] of the wealthy [leper]. And [the verse] “and upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering” [refers to that] of the poor [leper].

Rashi on Menachot 10a:2:2.hebrew: למה לי - כלומר, תרי קראי למה לי? בשלמא חד כתביה, לאשמועינן דיתן שמן על הדם ולא אצלו, אלא קרא דכתיב מקום דם למה לי:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:2:2.english: Why do I need - That is, why do I need two verses? Granted, one is written to teach us that he places the oil on the blood and not beside it; but why do I need [the verse that says] "the place of the blood"?

Rashi on Menachot 10a:3:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא איתיה אין - איתיה לדם, יתן השמן; אבל נתקנח הדם, לא יתן השמן:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:3:1.english: I would have said: If it is [there], yes - If the blood is [still] there, he should place the oil; but if the blood was wiped off, he should not place the oil.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:4:1.hebrew: הויא חציצה - בין שמן לבהן, וליפסל, דרחמנא אמר "על בהן", להכי איצטריך "על דם":
Rashi on Menachot 10a:4:1.english: It is an interposition - between the oil and the thumb, and [the placement] should be disqualified, since the Merciful One said "upon the thumb"; therefore "upon the blood" was necessary.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:5:1.hebrew: אמר רבא כו' וכתב ימנית בדם - למה לי למיהדר ולמכתב ימנית בשמן? לא לכתוב לא בעני ולא בעשיר! נהי דעל בהן יתירי איצטריכו דעני ודעשיר, להכשיר צדדין ולפסול צידי צדדין — אלא ימנית למה לי:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:5:1.english: Rava said, etc., and it is written "right" regarding the blood - Why do I need [the Torah] to go back and write "right" regarding the oil? Let it not be written, neither for the poor [leper] nor for the wealthy one! Granted, the additional [phrase] "upon the thumb" was needed for the poor [leper] and for the wealthy one, to validate the sides and to disqualify the sides of the sides — but "right," why do I need it?

Rashi on Menachot 10a:6:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - ליתא למאי דאפק' קמיצה דשמאל פסול מדרשת דארבעה שמאלית. דאם כן, ימנית דבין שמן דעשיר בין שמן דעני למה לי? אלא ימנית דשמן דעשיר, לההיא דרשה אתיא:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:6:1.english: Rather, Rava said - [The previous suggestion] is not so, [namely] that which we derived — that a handful taken with the left hand is invalid — from the exposition of the four [verses] about the left hand. For if so, why do I need the right [hand] stated both for the oil of the wealthy [leper] and for the oil of the poor [leper]? Rather, the right [hand] of the oil of the wealthy [leper] comes for that [other] exposition.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:6:2.hebrew: יד יד לקמיצה - כתיב במצורע עשיר "ידו הימנית" דלא איצטריך, וכתיב בקמיצה "יד": "וימלא כפו" (ויקרא ט׳:י״ז). מה יד מצורע ימנית, אף יד דקמיצה ימנית:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:6:2.english: "Hand" [and] "hand" for the removal of the handful - It is written regarding a wealthy leper, "his right hand," which is not needed [for its own law]; and it is written regarding the removal of the handful, "hand": "And he filled his hand" (Leviticus 9:17). Just as the hand of the leper is the right one, so too the hand [used] for the removal of the handful is the right one.

Rashi on Menachot 10a:7:1.hebrew: רגל - שמן דמצורע עשיר, למידרש חליצה בגזירה שוה דרגל רגל, דכתיב נמי בחליצה "וחלצה נעלו מעל רגלו" (דברים כ״ה:ט׳). מה רגל דמצורע ימנית, אף חליצה ימנית:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:7:1.english: Foot - [This refers to] the oil of a wealthy leper, [written] in order to derive [the law of] ḥalitza through the verbal analogy of “foot, foot,” as it is also written regarding ḥalitza: “And she shall remove his shoe from upon his foot” (Deuteronomy 25:9). Just as the foot of the leper is the right one, so too, in ḥalitza [it is the] right [foot].

Rashi on Menachot 10a:8:1.hebrew: ואוזן - דשמן עשיר דלא איצטריך, אתי למדרש "אזן אזן" דרציעה, דכתיב "ורצע אדניו את אזנו" (שמות כא): מה דמצורע ימנית, אף דרציעה ימנית. והך גזירה שוה מפורשת בפ"ק דקדושין (ד' טו.). ודעני לא דריש להו רבא, כדלקמן: כל פרשה שנאמרה ונשנית לא נשנית כו':
Rashi on Menachot 10a:8:1.english: And [the word] "ear" - Regarding the oil of a wealthy [leper], which is not needed [for its own teaching], it comes to be expounded [through the verbal analogy of] "ear, ear" of the piercing, as it is written: "And his master shall bore his ear through" (Exodus 21). Just as with the leper [the ear is] the right one, so too with the piercing [it is] the right one. And this verbal analogy is explained in the first chapter of Kiddushin (page 15a). And Rava does not expound these [verses] regarding a poor [leper], as [stated] below: "Any passage that was stated and repeated was not repeated [unless]..."

Rashi on Menachot 10a:9:1.hebrew: שמאלית למאי אתא - דעשיר לא איצטריך. למאי אתא? בשלמא קמא לגופיה — שמאלית ולא ימנית — אלא תניינא, למאי:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:9:1.english: The left [hand] — for what purpose does it come? - For the wealthy [leper] it is not needed. For what purpose does it come? Granted, the first [mention] is for its own sake — [it must be] the left hand and not the right — but the second, for what purpose [does it come]?

Rashi on Menachot 10a:9:2.hebrew: במקום שנתרבתה שמאל - כגון הכא דכתיב לעיל "שמאלית", כל שכן שנתרבתה ימין. להכי אתא "שמאלית" אחרינא בעשיר גופיה, דשינה עליו הכתוב לעכב שמאלית ולא ימנית. ואי קשיא הוי מיעוט אחר מיעוט, לאו פירכא היא, דשמאלית קמא לאו מיעוט הוא. דכיון דקיימא לן ג"ש דיד יד לקמיצה, הוה אמינא נמי נדרוש ג"ש האי כף דתיהוי ימנית, ואיצטריך למיכתב שמאל לאכשורי שמאל, ולעולם כל שכן ימין. להכי כתב רחמנא "שמאלית" אחרינא, למעוטי ימין:
Rashi on Menachot 10a:9:2.english: In a place where the left was included - For example, here, where it is written earlier "left," [then] all the more so is the right included. Therefore, another "left" came in the case of the wealthy [leper] himself, for the verse varied [its wording] with regard to him in order to restrict [the requirement] to the left and not the right. And if you raise the difficulty that this would be a limitation following a limitation, that is not a refutation, because the first "left" is not a limitation. For since we hold [that there is] a verbal analogy of "hand" [and] "hand" to the scooping [of the meal offering], I would have said that we should also derive by verbal analogy [that] this palm [of the priest] must be the right one, and it was necessary to write "left" to render the left valid, but in truth, all the more so [is] the right [valid]. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote another "left," to exclude the right.

Tosafot on Menachot 10a:2:1.hebrew: על דם האשם ועל מקום דם האשם למאי אתו - פירוש: דלכתוב או אידי ואידי "על מקום", או אידי ואידי "על דם":
Tosafot on Menachot 10a:2:1.english: "Upon the blood of the guilt offering" and "upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering" — for what purpose do they come? - Explanation: Let [the Torah] write either "upon the place" in both [cases], or "upon the blood" in both:

Tosafot on Menachot 10a:5:1.hebrew: אמר רבא מאחר דכתב על דם - כו' וכתיבא ימנית בדם על בהן ידו הימנית כו' למה לי. דנהי דעל בהן דעני ודעשיר צריכין לצדדין ולצידי צדדין, מ"מ ימנית למאי אתא? אלא אמר רבא: יד יד לקמיצה; יד ימנית דשמן דמצורע עשיר אתא לג"ש דקמיצה, ודמצורע עני — לפרשה שנאמרה לשנות. כך פירוש הסוגיא לפירוש הקונטרס. וקשה, דמשמע לרבא דימנית דדם איצטריך בין בעני בין בעשיר, ואמאי לא ילפי מהדדי כמו (נמי) בצדדין ובצידי צדדין? והוה לן למימר דימנית דדם דעני הוי לפרשה שנאמרה ונשנית, כמו ימנית דשמן דעני. ושמא לענין ימנית לא הוו ילפי אי לאו דהוו כתיבי בהדיא, כיון דחלוקין בקרבנותיהם, אע"ג דילפי מהדדי לצדדין ולצידי צדדין. עוד קשה, דמשמע שבא רבי ירמיה להקשות לרבי זירא, ולפירוש הקונטר' לא מקשי מידי. ועוד קשה, הא דלא נקט ר' ירמיה נמי תנוך אוזן. ועוד, כיון דר' ירמיה לא בעי על בהן למה לי אלא מכח דכתיב על דם האשם ועל מקום דם האשם, אם כן הוה ליה למימר: מאחר דכתיב על דם האשם ועל מקום דם האשם, על בהן למה לי, כדקאמר רבא. ונראה לפרש דפריך משום דדריש רבי זירא מכפו, דכל מקום שנאמר כף אינו אלא ימין; אם כן בעל בהן ידו, דהוי דומיא דכף, לא הוה צריך למכתב ימין. ולפי הספרים דגרסינן במצורע עשיר למה לי — לאו דוקא, והוא הדין דהוה פריך מצורע עני, אלא נקט עשיר משום דאפילו בעשיר קשיא ליה: אמאי איצטריך חד להכשיר צדדין וחד לפסול צידי צדדין? פירוש: ימנית דעשיר וימנית דעני. ואע"ג דימנית לא משמע לא צדדין ולא צידי צדדין, מייתורא בעלמא דריש. ובמילתיה דרבא גרסינן: מאחר דכתיב על דם האשם ועל מקום דם האשם, וכתב ימנית בדם של מצורע עשיר, ימנית דכתב בשמן דמצורע עני למה לי. ואיני יכול לישבו יפה, וצריך לדקדק בו:
Tosafot on Menachot 10a:5:1.english: Rava said: Since it is written "upon the blood" - etc. "And 'right' is written regarding the blood, 'upon the thumb of his right hand' etc., why do I need...?" For granted that [the verses of] "upon the thumb" of the poor person and of the wealthy person are needed for the sides and for the sides of the sides, nevertheless, for what purpose does "right" come? Rather, Rava said: [The word] "hand, hand" is [derived] from the *kemitzah* [handful]; the "right hand" of the oil of the wealthy leper comes for the verbal analogy [*gezerah shavah*] of the *kemitzah*, and that of the poor leper — for a passage that was stated and repeated. So is the explanation of the passage according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi]. But it is difficult, for it implies from Rava that the "right" of the blood was needed for both the poor and the wealthy; so why do they not derive from each other, just as [they do] (also) regarding the sides and the sides of the sides? And we should have said that the "right" of the blood of the poor person is [for] a passage that was stated and repeated, like the "right" of the oil of the poor person. And perhaps with regard to "right" they would not derive [from each other] had they not been written explicitly, since they differ in their offerings, even though they derive from each other for the sides and for the sides of the sides. Another difficulty: it implies that Rabbi Yirmeyah came to challenge Rabbi Zeira, yet according to the Kuntres's explanation he does not challenge anything. And further, it is difficult that Rabbi Yirmeyah did not also mention the cartilage of the ear. And further, since Rabbi Yirmeyah asks "why do I need 'upon the thumb'" only on account of the fact that it is written "upon the blood of the guilt offering" and "upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering," then he should have said: Since it is written "upon the blood of the guilt offering" and "upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering," why do I need "upon the thumb," as Rava said. And it appears to explain that he asks because Rabbi Zeira derives [it] from "his palm" — that anywhere "palm" is stated, it means only the right; if so, in "upon the thumb of his hand," which is similar to "palm," there would be no need to write "right." And according to the texts in which we read "why do I need [it] regarding the wealthy leper" — it is not precise, and equally he could have asked about the poor leper, but he mentioned the wealthy one because even regarding the wealthy one he finds it difficult: why was one needed to validate the sides and one to invalidate the sides of the sides? That is, the "right" of the wealthy person and the "right" of the poor person. And although "right" does not imply either the sides or the sides of the sides, he derives it merely from the superfluity. And in Rava's statement we read: Since it is written "upon the blood of the guilt offering" and "upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering," and it wrote "right" regarding the blood of the wealthy leper, why do I need the "right" that is written regarding the oil of the poor leper? But I cannot resolve it well, and it requires further examination:

Tosafot on Menachot 10a:9:1.hebrew: שמאל למאי אתא - משמאל שני דעשיר קא בעי, דקמא אתא לגופיה להכשיר שמאל. ומשני דאתא למעט ימין. ולמיעוט אחר מיעוט דנרבי ימין — אין לדרוש, דא"כ לא לכתוב אלא חד. והדר בעי: "ואידך שמאל למאי אתא", היינו דעני:
Tosafot on Menachot 10a:9:1.english: "The left – for what purpose does it come?" - [The Gemara] is asking about the second "left," that of the rich [leper], for the first came for its own sake, to validate [the use of] the left hand. And [Rav Sheisha] answers that it came to exclude the right hand. And as for [the possibility that this is] an exclusion following an exclusion, which would [serve] to include the right hand — one cannot expound [it that way], for if so, [the verse] should have written only one [mention of the left]. And afterward [the Gemara] asks: "And the other left, for what purpose does it come?" — that is, that of the poor [leper]:
